verdictReason: Killed. Every public listing of a plugin business with renewing licences starts near $30k (Flippa $30,000 for ~$6.7k revenue with 60% churn; Acquire $31,500 for $8.9k revenue; Flippa $149,300 for $47k), while the sub-$10k listings seen were lifetime-licence ($800) or pre-revenue ($6,480). At the lowest observed 3.2x revenue, $8.5k buys ~$2.7k revenue (~27 licences at $99/yr): operating profit ~$2.2k/yr (~$3.6/h), payback ~4 years, pessimistic -$9.2k. Free B2B cores (20,000+ installs) and GPL code leave no exclusive edge.

answers.question: Do sub-$10k WooCommerce/WordPress B2B-operations plugin businesses with >= 12 months of verifiable renewing licences exist for sale (the open question)?
answers.answer: No such listing was found, and the public listings show where the floor sits. Recurring-licence plugin businesses seen: Flippa portfolio of 50+ plugins asking USD $30,000 with ~$6.7k 2025 revenue, 80 active subscribers and 60% overall churn (D3); Acquire.com ratings plugin asking $31,500 with $8,873 annual revenue (D4); Flippa four-plugin WooCommerce business asking USD $149,300 on $46,950 revenue (D1, D2). Sub-$10k listings found were a Microns plugin asking $800 on $680 revenue with a lifetime licence and 36 customers, labelled 'Already Sold' (D5), and a pre-revenue WooCommerce plugin reduced to USD $6,480 (D6). None was a B2B-operations plugin. This cannot be proven absent: private broker lists and the paid tiers (FlipWP $299/yr, Acquire full financials) were not read (D16, B2B-1-E8), but the observed price floor of roughly 3.2x-4.5x revenue means a $10k budget only reaches businesses with about $2.5k-$3k of revenue.

answers.question: What renewal rates do WordPress/WooCommerce plugin licences actually get, and do they support buying an installed licence base?
answers.answer: Evidence is mixed and none is B2B-specific. Freemius's valuation guide calls a 'typical' business one with a renewal rate in the 50%+ range (D8). Toolset reported ~30% on manual renewals in 2018 (D9). A 2017 Freemius post cites developers reporting 60-80% after WooCommerce changed renewal rules, against 10% before (D10). The only listing with a stated figure shows 60% overall churn (D3). So a purchased annual-licence base can plausibly lose 40-70% of its renewing revenue each year unless the seller's new-sales engine (SEO, reviews, marketplace ranking) also transfers, which a stranger cannot assume.

answers.question: Do free or cheap alternatives already cover what a wholesale WooCommerce merchant needs from the premium add-on?
answers.answer: Largely yes. WooCommerce Wholesale Prices is free with 20,000+ active installs (D11). A WordPress.org B2B suite lists six free modules (access control, wholesale pricing with volume tiers and quick order, RFQ and quotes, registration approvals, analytics, automation) and a Pro add-on for net terms/CRM/ERP (D12). Paid options are cheap: WooCommerce.com B2B Pricing $99 for a 1-year plan (D14), Wholesale Suite $99/yr single site, $199 unlimited, $299 for the full five-plugin bundle (D13). At $99/yr, $2.7k of revenue is about 27 paying licences, which is a very thin base.

answers.question: Is there an exclusive or compounding edge for a stranger who buys such a plugin, and what would falsify it?
answers.answer: No structural edge was found. The WordPress.org listing and installs do transfer, but the handbook restricts larger plugins (B2B-1-E11), code must be GPL-compatible so rivals can fork it (B2B-1-E13), and another acquirer is openly buying: Bright Plugins runs 19+ premium plugins and says deals go 'from first call to payout in weeks, not months' (D15), so the entrant would bid against a faster, portfolio-scale buyer. WooCommerce.com Marketplace sellers also keep only 70% of sales and the transfer terms sit in a vendor agreement not read (D17). Falsifier: a public, verifiable listing of a B2B plugin at or below ~3x revenue with >= 60% renewal and a documented acquisition channel that survives a change of owner; none was found.

answers.question: What are the bottom-up first-365-day economics for the reference entrant ($10k, 12 h/week)?
answers.answer: Allocation (assumption): $8,500 purchase, $299 listing-access membership (D16), $500 legal/escrow/transfer admin, $350 running costs, 3% payment fees. Purchase multiple 3.2x revenue (lowest observed: $149,300 / $46,950 = 3.18x, D1) gives revenue ~$2,656 (D7 range 2-4x ARR; 2x would give $4,250). Year-1 cost $9,729, profit about -$7,073 including the purchase; operating profit (revenue minus running costs and fees) about $2,226, i.e. ~$3.6 per hour over 624 hours, payback ~4.2 years if revenue holds flat. Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, operating costs x1.5, purchase fixed): revenue ~$1,062, cost ~$10,271, profit ~-$9,209, operating profit ~$490 and payback ~19 years.

killReasons.reason: No public sign of sub-$10k supply for the wedge: recurring-licence plugin businesses are listed at $30,000 (~$6.7k revenue, 80 subscribers, 60% churn), $31,500 ($8.9k revenue) and $149,300 ($47k revenue); sub-$10k listings seen are lifetime-licence ($800) or pre-revenue ($6,480), and none is B2B-operations.

Economics fail even if supply existed: at 3.2x revenue (observed low; 2-4x ARR range) $8.5k buys ~$2.7k revenue, operating profit ~$2.2k/yr (~$3.6 per hour at 12 h/week), payback ~4 years, year-1 profit about -$7.1k; pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5) is about -$9.2k with ~19-year payback.

The purchased revenue base decays: renewal rates cited are ~30% (manual), 50%+ (valuation norm) and 60% churn on the one listing with a figure; at $99/yr per licence the base is only ~27 customers, and vendor pricing pages show renewal repricing risk ('all renewals are at full price').

No exclusive or compounding edge: free B2B cores with 20,000+ installs and a free six-module B2B suite cover the basics, GPL-compatible code can be forked, and an active portfolio acquirer closes deals in weeks.
Directory transfer of larger plugins is restricted and WooCommerce.com Marketplace sellers keep 70% with transfer terms in an unread vendor agreement, adding delay and margin risk.

assumptions: assumption: $8,500 of the $10,000 goes to the purchase price; the rest covers listing-access membership, legal/escrow/transfer admin and running costs

Purchase multiple 3.2x revenue = lowest observed (149,300 / 46,950 = 3.18x, B2B-1-D1); other observed: 31,500 / 8,873 = 3.55x (D4), 30,000 / 8,320 annualised = 3.6x (D3); Freemius range 2-4x ARR (D7). Revenue365 = 8,500 / 3.2 = about $2,656
assumption: seller's run-rate holds flat for the first 365 days (generous given 30-60% renewal evidence, D3/D8/D9); revenue arrives from inherited licence anniversaries, first revenue within ~90 days

FlipWP membership $299 (D16, 2021 price); assumption: $500 legal/escrow/transfer admin; assumption: $350 running costs (hosting, licence server, email, support desk; listings show far lower seller expenses but those exclude the buyer's tooling); assumption: 3% payment processing
Year-1 cost = 8,500 + 299 + 500 + 350 + 80 = $9,729; profit = -$7,073 including purchase; operating profit = 2,656 - 430 = $2,226 (~$3.6/h over 624 h)

Pessimistic: price x0.8 and volume x0.5 gives revenue ~$1,062; cost x1.5 applied to non-purchase costs (purchase price is a fixed contract amount, otherwise cost would exceed the $10k budget) gives cost ~$10,271 and profit ~-$9,209
Owner time (12 h/week) is not costed; ownership of the support and compatibility-testing workload is assumed possible at that time budget

legalNotes: WordPress.org: plugin transfer to a new owner is possible but larger plugins are restricted (B2B-1-E11); make any purchase conditional on the directory accepting the transfer.

WordPress.org guidelines: free plugins may not lock functionality behind payment (B2B-1-E12) and code must be GPL-compatible (B2B-1-E13), so a premium add-on has to be separate code and rivals may legally fork it.
WooCommerce.com Marketplace products are sold under a Marketplace Vendor Agreement with a 70% vendor share (D17); whether a product can be assigned to a new vendor was not read.

Transferring customer/licence databases may need a privacy-policy and data-processing review; acquisition-marketplace terms, fees and escrow rules (Flippa, Acquire.com, FlipWP) were not read. Not legal advice.
This research read only public pages with no logins, signups, purchases or contact with sellers; seller claims on listings are unaudited.
unverified: Whether any sub-$10k B2B-operations plugin with >= 12 months of renewing licences exists on private broker lists, in FlipWP's paid listings, or in Acquire.com's paid detail views; public pages cannot settle this and the sellers or brokers hold the data.
The renewal rate of any WooCommerce B2B plugin; the figures found are general WordPress plugin figures from 2017-2022 or a single listing, and none is audited.
Acquire.com listing 'WordPress plugin with 10K installs, recurring revenue, $29K TTM profit' could not be read (page returned no listing text), so its price and licence model are unknown.

Flippa listing 12279112 page fields show a 60% overall churn but do not say whether the subscriptions are annual licences; its stated revenue multiple (4.1x) differs from asking price divided by annualised revenue (3.6x).
WooCommerce.com Marketplace vendor-agreement transfer terms, WordPress.org transfer timing, and buyer fees on Flippa/Acquire.com were not read.
FlipWP membership price is from a 2021 article and may have changed; Freemius renewal figures are dated 2017-2022.
